Zhrnutie

  • Interest rate tightening: A net 43.8% of Slovak firms reported tighter loan interest rates, up 38.3 pp from a net 5.5% and now above the EA's net 40.0%, raising debt servicing costs.
  • Margin squeeze persists: Labour costs rose for a net 78.81% of Slovak firms, 19.85 pp above the EA, while a net 12.83% still reported declining turnover — compressing operating margins.
  • Weak demand outlook: Slovak firms' turnover expectations fell to a net 6.75%, trailing the euro area's net 25.88% by 19 pp and signalling weaker domestic demand ahead.
  • Credit line stress: The Slovak credit line gap rose to +15.3pp from +14.8pp as need outpaced near-neutral availability, leaving Slovak firms more stressed than the EA's +14.0pp.

Obsah

  • Podmienky financovania
    • Slovak firms reported a net 43.8% experiencing interest rate tightening in wave 39
    • Credit line stress persists as Slovak firm demand outpaces bank loan easing
    • Slovak firms' bank loan availability outlook diverged from improving EA trend
    • Slovak firms shifted toward fixed investment while working capital use remained elevated
    • Bank willingness to lend held steady for Slovak firms, above EA
  • Ekonomická situácia firiem

    • Slovak firms' turnover outlook fell sharply, diverging from euro area optimism
    • Slovak firms face margin compression as input costs outpace selling prices
    • Slovak firms' upside inflation risk bias widened against the euro area trend

Podmienky financovania

Slovak firms reported a net 43.8% experiencing interest rate tightening in wave 39

Changes in Terms and Conditions of Bank Financing (Q10)

  • A net 43.8% of Slovak firms (n=76) reported tighter interest rates, up 38.3 pp from 5.5% in the prior wave, now above EA (40.0%) and DE (42.5%) — raising debt servicing costs.
  • A net 12.4% of Slovak firms (n=74) reported smaller available loan or credit line sizes, rising 6.3 pp from the previous wave, exceeding the EA (net 9.1%) and DE (net 7.9%) — limiting liquidity buffers.
  • Loan maturity conditions tightened for a net 11.6% of Slovak firms (n=76), compared with a net 4.4% in the EA and net 3.4% in DE — reducing financial flexibility.

* Túto otázku dostávajú iba firmy, ktoré v minulosti využili alebo žiadali o daný typ financovania. Nižší počet respondentov oproti celkovej vzorke je zámerný a neindikuje problém s kvalitou dát — pozri metodológiu ECB SAFE.

ⓘ SQL — bank_loan_terms.sql (cited column: net_balance_wtd)
-- Chart 1: Changes in terms and conditions of bank financing (Q10)
-- Countries: Slovakia (SK), Euro Area (EA), Austria (AT), Germany (DE)
-- All firm sizes combined (firm_size = 'all'), last 4 waves
--
-- net_balance_wtd: positive = net tightening (adverse for firms)
--                 negative = net easing (favourable for firms)
-- Sub-items:
--   a = Level of interest rates
--   b = Non-interest financing costs (charges, fees, commissions)
--   c = Available size of loan or credit line
--   d = Available maturity of the loan
--   e = Collateral requirements
--   f = Other terms (guarantees, covenants, procedures)

WITH latest_waves AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT wave_number
    FROM main_safe.mart_safe__financing_conditions
    WHERE question_id = 'q10'
    ORDER BY wave_number DESC
    LIMIT 4
)

SELECT
    f.wave_number,
    f.survey_period_label,
    f.country_code,
    f.sub_item,
    f.sub_item_label,
    f.net_balance_wtd,
    f.pct_improved_wtd,
    f.pct_deteriorated_wtd,
    f.pct_unchanged_wtd,
    f.n_respondents
FROM main_safe.mart_safe__financing_conditions f
WHERE f.question_id = 'q10'
  AND f.country_code IN ('SK', 'EA', 'DE')
  AND f.firm_size = 'all'
  AND f.wave_number IN (SELECT wave_number FROM latest_waves)
ORDER BY f.sub_item, f.country_code, f.wave_number

Credit line stress persists as Slovak firm demand outpaces bank loan easing

Financing Need vs Availability Gap (Q5/Q9)

  • The Slovak credit line gap rose to +15.3pp (n=270) from +14.8pp in the previous wave, driven by rising need (+15.2pp) with availability near neutral (-0.1pp), leaving Slovak firms more stressed than the EA (+14.0pp).
  • The Slovak trade credit gap swung from +6.3pp to -1.7pp (n=180), as need fell from +7.1pp to -3.4pp, placing Slovak firms less stressed than the EA (+11.0pp).
  • The Slovak bank loan gap deepened to -6.0pp (n=214) from -4.0pp in the previous wave, driven by improved availability (+5.6pp), leaving Slovak firms less stressed than the EA (+2.8pp).

* Túto otázku dostávajú iba firmy, ktoré v minulosti využili alebo žiadali o daný typ financovania. Nižší počet respondentov oproti celkovej vzorke je zámerný a neindikuje problém s kvalitou dát — pozri metodológiu ECB SAFE.

ⓘ SQL — financing_gap.sql (cited column: financing_gap_wtd)
-- Financing need vs availability gap (Q5/Q9) from mart_safe__financing_conditions
-- financing_gap_wtd = Q5 net balance (need) minus Q9 net balance (availability)
-- Positive gap = need exceeds availability (adverse for firms)
-- Countries: Slovakia (SK), Euro Area (EA), Germany (DE)
-- All firms (firm_size = 'all'), last 4 waves (dynamic)
--
-- Returns two result sets unioned:
--   type='main'  — bank loans (sub_item='a') for SK/EA/DE — used for the main grouped-bar chart
--   type='sk_all' — all major instruments for SK only — used for the SK instrument breakdown chart

WITH latest_waves AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT wave_number
    FROM main_safe.mart_safe__financing_conditions
    WHERE question_id = 'q9'
    ORDER BY wave_number DESC
    LIMIT 4
),

q5 AS (
    SELECT wave_number, survey_period_label, country_code, sub_item, sub_item_label,
           net_balance_wtd AS need_nb, n_respondents AS n_respondents_need
    FROM main_safe.mart_safe__financing_conditions
    WHERE question_id = 'q5'
      AND country_code IN ('SK', 'EA', 'DE')
      AND firm_size = 'all'
      AND wave_number IN (SELECT wave_number FROM latest_waves)
),

q9 AS (
    SELECT wave_number, country_code, sub_item,
           net_balance_wtd        AS availability_nb,
           financing_gap_wtd,
           n_respondents          AS n_respondents_avail
    FROM main_safe.mart_safe__financing_conditions
    WHERE question_id = 'q9'
      AND country_code IN ('SK', 'EA', 'DE')
      AND firm_size = 'all'
      AND wave_number IN (SELECT wave_number FROM latest_waves)
),

joined AS (
    SELECT
        q5.wave_number,
        q5.survey_period_label,
        q5.country_code,
        q5.sub_item,
        q5.sub_item_label,
        q5.need_nb,
        q9.availability_nb,
        q9.financing_gap_wtd,
        q5.n_respondents_need,
        q9.n_respondents_avail
    FROM q5
    JOIN q9 USING (wave_number, country_code, sub_item)
)

-- Main chart: bank loans (a), credit lines (f), trade credit (b) for SK/EA/DE
SELECT *, 'main' AS chart_type
FROM joined
WHERE sub_item IN ('a', 'f', 'b')

UNION ALL

-- SK instrument breakdown: all instruments for Slovakia only
SELECT *, 'sk_all' AS chart_type
FROM joined
WHERE country_code = 'SK'
  AND sub_item IN ('a', 'b', 'f', 'g', 'h')

ORDER BY chart_type, sub_item, country_code, wave_number

Slovak firms' bank loan availability outlook diverged from improving EA trend

Expected Availability of External Financing (Q23)

  • A net 6.46% of Slovak firms (n=104) expected bank loan availability to worsen in wave 39, down 1.30 pp from wave 38, while the EA improved 1.45 pp to 2.35%, signalling tighter conditions ahead.
  • Credit line availability expectations eased by 3.16 pp to a net 3.87% of Slovak firms (n=136) expecting deterioration—compared with a net 2.25% for the EA, still pointing to cautious lender behavior.
  • Trade credit pessimism receded, with a net 6.18% of Slovak firms (n=90) expecting deterioration—improving by 4.04 pp from wave 38's net 10.22%, though remaining above the EA's net 1.87%, limiting supplier-backed financing options.

* Túto otázku dostávajú iba firmy, ktoré v minulosti využili alebo žiadali o daný typ financovania. Nižší počet respondentov oproti celkovej vzorke je zámerný a neindikuje problém s kvalitou dát — pozri metodológiu ECB SAFE.

† Bunky s menej ako 10 platnými odpoveďami v danej kombinácii vlny × krajiny × položky sú vynechané z grafu; medzery v sérii indikujú nedostatok dát pre dané obdobie.

ⓘ SQL — availability_expectations.sql (cited column: net_balance_wtd)
-- Q23: Expected availability of external financing over the next quarter
-- Countries: Slovakia (SK), Euro Area (EA), Germany (DE)
-- All firms (firm_size = 'all'), last 4 waves (dynamic)
--
-- net_balance_wtd: % expecting improvement minus % expecting deterioration
-- Positive = more firms expect availability to IMPROVE (FAVOURABLE)
-- Negative = more firms expect availability to DETERIORATE (ADVERSE)
--
-- Sub-items (matching Q5/Q9 instruments):
--   b = Bank loans
--   d = Trade credit
--   g = Credit lines and bank overdraft

WITH latest_waves AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT wave_number
    FROM main_safe.mart_safe__availability_expectations
    ORDER BY wave_number DESC
    LIMIT 4
)

SELECT
    f.wave_number,
    f.survey_period_label,
    f.country_code,
    f.sub_item,
    f.sub_item_label,
    f.net_balance_wtd,
    f.pct_improve_wtd,
    f.pct_deteriorate_wtd,
    f.n_respondents
FROM main_safe.mart_safe__availability_expectations f
WHERE f.country_code IN ('SK', 'EA', 'DE')
  AND f.firm_size = 'all'
  AND f.n_respondents >= 10
  AND f.wave_number IN (SELECT wave_number FROM latest_waves)
ORDER BY f.sub_item, f.country_code, f.wave_number

Slovak firms shifted toward fixed investment while working capital use remained elevated

Purpose of Financing (Q6A)

  • Fixed investment citation rose from 34.2% to 40.7% among Slovak firms (n=242), a 6.5 pp increase that brought Slovakia above the euro area's 38.4% — suggesting stronger long-term growth capacity.
  • Inventory and working capital remained the dominant financing purpose for Slovak firms (n=242) at 57.0%, 16.2 pp above the euro area's 40.8% — highlighting persistent liquidity needs.
  • The share of Slovak firms (n=241) citing refinancing or paying off obligations fell from 21.5% to 17.0%, easing 4.5 pp from the previous wave.
ⓘ SQL — financing_purpose.sql (cited column: pct_cited_wtd)
-- Q6A: Purpose of financing (multi-select)
-- pct_cited_wtd = % of firms citing each purpose (can sum > 100% as multi-select)
-- purposes: 1=Fixed investment, 2=Inventory/working capital, 3=Hiring/training,
--           4=New products/services, 5=Refinancing, 6=Other
-- Countries: Slovakia (SK), Euro Area (EA), Germany (DE)
-- All firms (firm_size = 'all'), last 4 waves (dynamic)

WITH latest_waves AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT wave_number
    FROM main_safe.mart_safe__financing_purpose
    ORDER BY wave_number DESC
    LIMIT 4
)

SELECT
    f.wave_number,
    f.survey_period_label,
    f.country_code,
    f.purpose_id,
    f.purpose_label,
    f.pct_cited_wtd,
    f.n_respondents
FROM main_safe.mart_safe__financing_purpose f
WHERE f.country_code IN ('SK', 'EA', 'DE')
  AND f.firm_size = 'all'
  AND f.wave_number IN (SELECT wave_number FROM latest_waves)
ORDER BY f.purpose_id, f.country_code, f.wave_number

Bank willingness to lend held steady for Slovak firms, above EA

Factors Affecting Access to External Financing (Q11)

  • A net 7.8% of Slovak firms (n=310) reported an improvement in banks' willingness to provide credit, unchanged from the previous wave and outpacing the EA's net 5.6% — suggesting easier financing conditions.
  • The general economic outlook deteriorated for a net 51.6% of Slovak firms (n=472), down 7.2 pp from the prior wave and 22.2 pp below the EA net of 29.4%, pressuring credit demand.
  • Access to public financial support improved for Slovak firms (n=310), with the net balance rising from -33.8% (wave 38) to -21.2% (wave 39), though conditions remained adverse.
ⓘ SQL — financing_factors.sql (cited column: net_balance_wtd)
-- Q11: Self-assessed factors affecting availability of external financing
-- Net balance = % reporting improvement minus % reporting deterioration
-- Positive = factor improving (favourable for financing access)
-- Negative = factor deteriorating (adverse / potential credit supply constraint)
--
-- Key sub-items for credit supply analysis:
--   f = Willingness of banks to provide credit  (direct bank supply signal)
--   a = General economic outlook                (macro drag on supply)
--   b = Access to public financial support      (policy/guarantee channel)
--
-- Countries: Slovakia (SK), Euro Area (EA), Germany (DE)
-- All firms (firm_size = 'all'), last 4 waves (dynamic)

WITH latest_waves AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT wave_number
    FROM main_safe.mart_safe__financing_factors
    ORDER BY wave_number DESC
    LIMIT 4
)

SELECT
    f.wave_number,
    f.survey_period_label,
    f.country_code,
    f.sub_item,
    f.sub_item_label,
    f.net_balance_wtd,
    f.pct_improved_wtd,
    f.pct_deteriorated_wtd,
    f.n_respondents
FROM main_safe.mart_safe__financing_factors f
WHERE f.country_code IN ('SK', 'EA', 'DE')
  AND f.firm_size = 'all'
  AND f.sub_item IN ('f', 'a', 'b')
  AND f.wave_number IN (SELECT wave_number FROM latest_waves)
ORDER BY f.sub_item, f.country_code, f.wave_number

Ekonomická situácia firiem

Slovak turnover improved but remained negative, lagging the euro area

Business Situation Indicators (Q2)

  • A net 12.83% of Slovak firms (n=242) reported declining turnover in wave 39, improving 13.39 pp from wave 38, yet still contrasting with the EA's net 8.11% increase — suggesting weaker demand.
  • A net 34.38% of Slovak firms (n=242) reported falling profits, improving 5.42 pp from wave 38, while the EA's net decline stood at 15.39% — a gap of around 19 pp — limiting investment capacity.
  • Labour cost pressures remained elevated, with a net 78.81% of Slovak firms (n=242) reporting increases — 19.85 pp above the EA net — squeezing margins further.
ⓘ SQL — business_situation.sql (cited column: net_balance_wtd)
-- Q2: Business situation indicators (turnover, labour costs, profit, investment, employees)
-- Countries: Slovakia (SK), Euro Area (EA), Germany (DE)
-- All firms (firm_size = 'all'), last 4 waves (dynamic)
--
-- sub_items: a=Turnover, b=Labour costs, e=Profit, g=Investment, i=Employees
-- Sign: positive = indicator rising; labour costs positive = costs rising (adverse)

WITH latest_waves AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT wave_number
    FROM main_safe.mart_safe__business_situation
    ORDER BY wave_number DESC
    LIMIT 4
)

SELECT
    f.wave_number,
    f.survey_period_label,
    f.country_code,
    f.sub_item,
    f.sub_item_label,
    f.net_balance_wtd,
    f.pct_increased_wtd,
    f.pct_decreased_wtd,
    f.n_respondents
FROM main_safe.mart_safe__business_situation f
WHERE f.country_code IN ('SK', 'EA', 'DE')
  AND f.firm_size = 'all'
  AND f.wave_number IN (SELECT wave_number FROM latest_waves)
ORDER BY f.sub_item, f.country_code, f.wave_number

Slovak firms' turnover outlook fell sharply, diverging from euro area optimism

Expected Changes in Turnover and Investment (Q26)

  • Slovak firms' turnover expectations fell to a net 6.75% (n=228), trailing the euro area's net 25.88% by 19 pp in wave 38 — signalling weaker domestic demand.
  • Slovak turnover expectations declined by 14 pp from a net 20.90% two waves earlier, while the euro area's outlook rose from net 23.16% to net 25.88% — highlighting a growing competitiveness gap.
  • Fixed investment expectations bucked the turnover trend, rising to a net 14.67% (n=228) — above the euro area's net 9.45% — up 3.88 pp from the previous wave.

‡ Táto otázka sa nekladie každý štvrťrok — susedné body v grafe môžu byť vzdialené viac než jeden štvrťrok. Skutočné obdobie zisťovania nájdete v popiskoch bodov.

ⓘ SQL — outlook.sql (cited column: net_balance_wtd)
-- Q26: Expected changes in turnover and investments over the next two quarters
-- Countries: Slovakia (SK), Euro Area (EA), Germany (DE)
-- All firms (firm_size = 'all'), last 4 waves (dynamic)
--
-- net_balance_wtd: positive = more firms expect increase (FAVOURABLE)
--                 negative = more firms expect decrease (ADVERSE)
-- Sub-items:
--   a = Company's turnover
--   b = Investments in property, plant or equipment

WITH latest_waves AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT wave_number
    FROM main_safe.mart_safe__outlook
    ORDER BY wave_number DESC
    LIMIT 4
)

SELECT
    f.wave_number,
    f.survey_period_label,
    f.country_code,
    f.sub_item,
    f.sub_item_label,
    f.net_balance_wtd,
    f.pct_increase_wtd,
    f.pct_decrease_wtd,
    f.n_respondents
FROM main_safe.mart_safe__outlook f
WHERE f.country_code IN ('SK', 'EA', 'DE')
  AND f.firm_size = 'all'
  AND f.wave_number IN (SELECT wave_number FROM latest_waves)
ORDER BY f.sub_item, f.country_code, f.wave_number

Slovak firms face margin compression as input costs outpace selling prices

Price, Wage and Employment Expectations (Q31/Q34)

  • Slovak firms (n=224) expected production input prices to rise 7.33% — versus only 3.75% for selling prices (n=222) and 5.35% across the EA, pointing to continued margin compression.
  • Slovak firms (n=233) anticipated 4.12% average wage growth over the next 12 months, compared with 2.60% across the EA (n=4,941), adding further cost pressure.
  • Twelve-month inflation expectations among Slovak firms (n=193) eased to 4.68% from 4.97% in the previous wave, remaining 0.80 pp above the EA mean of 3.88%.

† Bunky s menej ako 10 platnými odpoveďami v danej kombinácii vlny × krajiny × položky sú vynechané z grafu; medzery v sérii indikujú nedostatok dát pre dané obdobie.

ⓘ SQL — expectations_quantitative.sql (cited column: mean_wtd)
-- Q31/Q34: Quantitative expectations — inflation rate (Q31) and expected % changes
-- in selling prices, input costs, wages, employment (Q34).
-- Countries: Slovakia (SK), Euro Area (EA), Germany (DE)
-- All firms (firm_size = 'all'), last 4 waves (dynamic)
--
-- mean_wtd: weighted mean expected % change (NOT a net balance)
-- Positive = firms expect an increase; negative = firms expect a decrease.
--
-- Sub-items:
--   Q31_a = Expected inflation rate in 12 months
--   Q34_a = Average selling price of products/services
--   Q34_b = Average prices of production inputs (non-labour)
--   Q34_c = Average wage of employees
--   Q34_d = Number of employees
--
-- panel_id = question_id || '_' || sub_item to disambiguate Q31/Q34 sub_item 'a'

WITH latest_waves AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT wave_number
    FROM main_safe.mart_safe__expectations
    WHERE question_id = 'q34'
    ORDER BY wave_number DESC
    LIMIT 4
)

SELECT
    f.wave_number,
    f.survey_period_label,
    f.country_code,
    f.question_id,
    f.sub_item,
    f.question_id || '_' || f.sub_item                          AS panel_id,
    f.sub_item_label,
    f.mean_wtd,
    f.p25_unwtd,
    f.median_unwtd,
    f.p75_unwtd,
    f.n_respondents
FROM main_safe.mart_safe__expectations f
WHERE f.country_code IN ('SK', 'EA', 'DE')
  AND f.firm_size = 'all'
  AND f.question_id IN ('q31', 'q34')
  AND f.sub_item IN ('a', 'b', 'c', 'd')
  AND f.mean_wtd IS NOT NULL
  AND f.n_respondents >= 10
  AND f.wave_number IN (SELECT wave_number FROM latest_waves)
ORDER BY f.question_id, f.sub_item, f.country_code, f.wave_number

Slovak firms' upside inflation risk bias widened against the euro area trend

Inflation Risk Outlook (Q33)

  • A net 61.2% of Slovak firms (n=242) saw inflation risks skewed to the upside over five years—suggesting heightened pricing pressure expectations.
  • Slovakia’s net upside inflation risk balance rose from 58.9% in the previous wave to 61.2%, moving in the opposite direction to the euro area, which eased from 55.3% to 54.0%.
  • The SK–EA gap on long-run upside inflation risk widened from 3.6 pp to 7.2 pp across consecutive waves—indicating diverging inflation perceptions.

† Bunky s menej ako 10 platnými odpoveďami v danej kombinácii vlny × krajiny × položky sú vynechané z grafu; medzery v sérii indikujú nedostatok dát pre dané obdobie.

ⓘ SQL — expectations_risk.sql (cited column: net_balance_wtd)
-- Q33: Main risk to 5-year inflation outlook (ordinal net balance)
-- Countries: Slovakia (SK), Euro Area (EA), Germany (DE)
-- All firms (firm_size = 'all'), last 4 waves (dynamic)
--
-- net_balance_wtd: % seeing upside inflation risk minus % seeing downside risk
-- Positive = more firms see inflation as a risk to the upside
-- Negative = more firms see inflation risk to the downside

WITH latest_waves AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT wave_number
    FROM main_safe.mart_safe__expectations
    WHERE question_id = 'q33'
    ORDER BY wave_number DESC
    LIMIT 4
)

SELECT
    f.wave_number,
    f.survey_period_label,
    f.country_code,
    f.pct_downside_wtd,
    f.pct_balanced_wtd,
    f.pct_upside_wtd,
    f.net_balance_wtd,
    f.n_respondents
FROM main_safe.mart_safe__expectations f
WHERE f.country_code IN ('SK', 'EA', 'DE')
  AND f.firm_size = 'all'
  AND f.question_id = 'q33'
  AND f.n_respondents >= 10
  AND f.wave_number IN (SELECT wave_number FROM latest_waves)
ORDER BY f.country_code, f.wave_number

Skilled staff and production costs dominate Slovak firms' business concerns

Most Pressing Business Problems (Q0B)

  • Among the seven problems tested, skilled staff availability was the top concern for Slovak firms (n=239), scoring 6.64/10 — up 0.57 points from wave 38, exceeding the EA's 6.57/10, highlighting a growing talent gap.
  • Costs of production or labour ranked second at 6.62/10 (n=240), rising 0.43 points from wave 38, just below the EA score of 6.74/10, squeezing margins further.
  • Regulation scored 6.10/10 (n=236), easing marginally by 0.08 points from wave 38, yet remaining above the EA average of 5.87/10, still burdening compliance efforts.
ⓘ SQL — business_problems.sql (cited column: avg_pressingness_wtd)
-- Q0B: Most pressing business problems
-- Countries: Slovakia (SK), Euro Area (EA), Germany (DE)
-- All firms (firm_size = 'all'), last 4 waves (dynamic)

WITH latest_waves AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT wave_number
    FROM main_safe.mart_safe__business_problems
    ORDER BY wave_number DESC
    LIMIT 4
)

SELECT
    f.wave_number,
    f.survey_period_label,
    f.country_code,
    f.problem_id,
    f.problem_label,
    f.avg_pressingness_wtd,
    f.n_respondents
FROM main_safe.mart_safe__business_problems f
WHERE f.country_code IN ('SK', 'EA', 'DE')
  AND f.firm_size = 'all'
  AND f.wave_number IN (SELECT wave_number FROM latest_waves)
ORDER BY f.problem_id, f.country_code, f.wave_number

Zdroj: ECB SAFE mikrodáta. Čistá bilancia = % podnikov hlásiacich nárast mínus % podnikov hlásiacich pokles. Kladná hodnota = sprísnenie / rast (nepriaznivé pre firmy, ak nie je uvedené inak). Záporná hodnota = uvoľnenie / pokles.
